title: Bondman
summary: One issue of a magazine for readers who can’t read well yet. Made for fans of a cartoon spy, so a six-year-old can find every puzzle without help.
coverAlt: Magazine cover with a cartoon spy and bold, easy navigation

blocks.heading: The idea
blocks.body: Young readers navigate by picture and color long before they read words. Every section has its own color and its own symbol, so a child can say “the blue pages” and find the puzzles.

blocks.label: Research. Reading sessions with first graders, and notes on what they pointed at first.

blocks.heading: Process
blocks.body: I tested three covers with a class of first graders. They ignored the title and went straight for the character’s face, so the final cover gives the face most of the page and keeps the words short.

blocks.caption: Three covers, tested with readers aged five to seven.

blocks.heading: Reflection
blocks.body: Children are honest reviewers. Next time I would bring them in at the sketch stage, not after the first draft.
